title: Higher fines for loud vehicle sound systems
summary: On July 7 the council held a roll call on the vehicle noise bill, Bill 119; the facts do not give the result. On June 19 it released the bill from committee, 8-0, and passed an amendment 7-2 that raises noise fines. The revised version drops forfeiture of sound systems for a third offense, and the chair said state law caps these fines at $1,000.

boards.name: Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The council postponed a proposed change to noise violation penalties until it takes up a related committee report.
The amendment passed with seven ayes and two noes.
The chair moved to replace Bill 119 with a version that raises fines for noise violations.
The council voted eight ayes, zero noes to discharge, or release, Bill 119 from committee.
The committee voted five ayes, with four members excused, to discharge Bill 119-2025.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: Chair Lee said the discharge moves the bill to the full council.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The deputy prosecuting attorney said he has not seen anyone fight a noise ticket in court in 15 years.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: A police sergeant said he could look into how many noise citations were given in the last year.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: Chair Lee, who introduced the bill, said loud music is a problem in Wailuku and asked members to pass it.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The deputy prosecuting attorney said unpaid fines block people from renewing their driver's license.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: A deputy prosecuting attorney said the department supports the revised version without forfeiture.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The chair said state law does not allow fines for these violations to go above $1,000.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The committee chair prepared a revised version, called CD1, that removes forfeiture from the third offense and raises fines for first and second offenses.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The bill would raise fines for loud vehicle sound systems and allow the systems to be taken away, called forfeiture.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: One person testified that the fines seemed too high for poor people.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The committee had one item: Bill 119-2025, about penalties for prohibited noise violations.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee
